children: Our Bureau Mumbai: The ownership dispute at electrical goods maker GreatWhite Global has ended with Mehul Jadavji Shah's family acquiring the 50% stake held by his younger brother Hemang Jadavji Shah's family for about 862 crore. The deal ends Hemang Shah's 15-year entrepreneurial association with the business, which he helped build into a significant player in electrical switches and automation.

The brothers, who hold equal stakes in GreatWhite Global, have fought over control for more than a year. On January 29, ET reported a family agreement under which Hemang decided to transfer his 50% stake to his elder brother, Mehul Shah. The company reported revenue of 1,284 crore and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) of over 131 crore in FY25.

The Shah family launched GreatWhite Electricals after selling the Anchor switch brand to Panasonic (then Matsushita Electric Works) for around Rs 2,000 crore in 2007. GreatWhite was launched in 2011, soon after Anchor Group's non-compete agreement with the Japanese firm ended.

Disputes between the brothers over management and operations landed in court with Hemang Shah approaching the National Company Law Tribunal in November 2024 and alleging oppression and mismanagement. During the resolution process, Hemang Shah accepted a counterbid from Mehul Shah's family and opted to exit.

The transaction ends the family conflict and places the company under single ownership. Munaf Virjee of AMR Law, DSK Legal and Fusion Capital Advisors acted as legal and financial advisors to Hemang Shah and his family, while ICICI Securities and Aditya Mehta and Shivani Garg of Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas advised Mehul Shah and his family.

Edelweiss Alternative Asset Advisors (EAAA) financed the transaction through a structured finance deal. According to the consent terms filed by the parties, EAAA India Alternatives funded it through India Special Assets Fund III, ISAF III Offshore Fund, and Special Situation India Fund.

title: GreatWhite Family Settles Row with Mehul Shah Buying Kin's 50% Stake
